item.title: Pennsylvania couple accidentally bought an 1830s house for $460,000; 5 years and $300,000 later, it is 85% complete
item.description: A Pennsylvania couple, Tyler and Lauren Bouldin, bought an abandoned stone house at an auction for $460,000. They faced numerous challenges during renovations, including structural issues and rising costs due to the pandemic. The couple decided to shift their approach to reuse materials and take on more work themselves. After about five years of work, the renovations are approximately 85% complete, although challenges remain.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Jelly Roll and Bunnie Xo list $7M Tennessee home after divorce
item.description: Country singer Jelly Roll, whose real name is Jason DeFord, and Bunnie Xo are selling their Tennessee home. They finalized their divorce settlement earlier this year, transferring ownership of the property to Bunnie Xo. The mansion sits on nearly 10 acres and was built in 2022, with an asking price of around $7 million.

item.title: In 1925, a Yellowstone explosion reshaped Biscuit Basin; 101 years later, USGS found a sign mix-up
item.description: A captivating century-old enigma surrounds Yellowstone's Biscuit Basin, centering on the misplacement of Black Pearl Geyser. The confusion stemmed from a hydrothermal explosion in 1925, which not only reshaped the landscape but also displaced a key sign. Correspondence from 1926 highlighted the depth of this perplexity related to the geyser's position.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Pregnant mum won £1m lottery, then welcomed her baby four days later
item.description: In February 2019, Natalie and Andrew Symes unexpectedly won £1 million in the EuroMillions lottery. Shortly after their win, they welcomed their daughter Poppy a month earlier than expected. The couple used their winnings to buy a home and relieve financial pressure during lockdowns. Natalie's ability to stay home with the children has been a significant change in their lives.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Kansas neighbour cut 133 trees, some 70 feet onto adjoining land; court upholds $6,500 award
item.description: A Kansas appeals court has upheld a $6,500 damages award against a man whose neighbour’s fence project led to 133 trees being cut on adjoining land in 2015. The court found the landowner filed his trespass case within the legal time limit and that there was enough evidence to hold Douglas Black responsible for the tree damage.

item.title: 18 skulls excavated from Egypt’s First Dynasty cemetery offer evidence of retainer sacrifice
item.description: Researchers re-examininf 46 skulls excavated from Egypt’s First Dynasty royal cemetery at Abydos, found significant cranial trauma in 18 of them. The injuries provide new forensic evidence that some people buried around royal tombs may have been deliberately killed after a ruler’s death. The findings support the possibility of retainer sacrifice, although the exact cause of death remains uncertain for many others.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: France school protests: 15-year-old student loses hand in stun grenade incident
item.description: Protests in France have intensified due to teacher shortages, resulting in widespread school closures and clashes. A 15-year-old student lost his hand after handling a police stun grenade, prompting a government investigation. Police reported numerous arrests and significant property damage since the protests began last week. Student unions continue to organise demonstrations despite concerns over escalating violence.
item.dc:creator: Karan Manral

item.title: Operation 'Yemen Dawn': Saudi-led coalition joins fight to wrest Red Sea from Houthis
item.description: Saudi military spokesman Maj. Gen. Turki al-Malki said the coalition was providing “full operational support” to government forces. He said around 100 fighter jets were supporting the campaign and that the coalition had established “air protection” over the strategic Bab el-Mandeb Strait. The coalition also claimed to have destroyed hundreds of Houthi targets. Those claims, however, could not be independently verified.
item.dc:creator: Rajeev Singh

item.title: Tiger Woods helps launch $2.5 billion Texas golf community with homes starting at $1 million
item.description: Tiger Woods is helping launch Bluejack Ranch, a $2.5 billion, 914-acre gated golf community near Fort Worth, Texas. The project will have 500 homes, an 18-hole course, a dude ranch and resort-style amenities, with residential prices starting at $1 million.

item.title: Your gut bacteria may reveal how quickly your brain is ageing; it effects memory, focus and mood
item.description: A groundbreaking study by UCLA Health highlights the intriguing link between gut bacteria and brain ageing in healthy adults. Analyzing brain scans and gut health of nearly 1,500 participants, researchers identified a correlation between the Brain Ageing Index and certain gut microbes. This suggests that optimizing gut health may be pivotal for preserving cognitive function and offers an early detection path for interventions aimed at promoting healthier brain ageing.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Kelowna grower Abbate’s giant pumpkin weighing 1,485 pounds, wins British Columbia’s 2026 contest
item.description: Kelowna grower Jordan Abbate won the 2026 B.C. Giant Pumpkin Contest with a 1,485-pound pumpkin, beating the runner-up by just one pound. The victory followed six months of daily care, including watering, pruning and soil preparation. The contest also saw two new B.C. records in other giant vegetable categories.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Scientists develop a living building material for Mars using engineered yeast
item.description: Researchers have developed an innovative living building material designed for potential use on Mars, integrating engineered yeast with sand. This breakthrough material operates with significantly lower energy requirements than traditional high-temperature construction methods. Tests indicate that existing bricks retain their integrity and the yeast's viability, promoting sustainability. While the engineered yeast does reinforce the material's strength and structure, additional evaluation is needed to determine its enduring durability in Martian conditions.
